Home News Region Girl, 8, dies of severe dengue in Bacolod News Region Girl, 8, dies of severe dengue in Bacolod By Mae Singuay - Thursday, October 15, 2026 Facebook X Viber Print BACOLOD City — An eight-year-old girl from Barangay Handumanan died of severe dengue, bringing the city’s dengue-related fatalities to six as infections increased by 1.5 percent from last year’s figure, the City Health Office (CHO) reported. The child died on October 3 after suffering complications, including dengue hemorrhagic shock, pulmonary hemorrhage and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome. She was admitted to a hospital on October 1 after experiencing persistent fever, vomiting and abdominal pain, followed by diarrhea. According to the CHO, the girl had previously been hospitalized for dengue at the age of five, making her latest infection her second encounter with the mosquito-borne disease. She developed a high fever on September 28, which temporarily subsided after she was given paracetamol. She initially consulted a private clinic and was diagnosed with a urinary tract infection before her condition worsened. Laboratory results on October 1 showed that her platelet count had dropped to 34,000, indicating a dangerously low level. Despite hospitalization, her condition continued to deteriorate, and she suffered cardiopulmonary arrest on October 3. She was pronounced dead at around 10:30 a.m. The CHO said the fatality was reported to the office on October 4. The latest death brings to six the number of dengue-related fatalities recorded in Bacolod as of Morbidity Week 39, covering September 27 to October 3. The city recorded 891 dengue cases during the period, up 1.5 percent from the 878 cases reported during the same period in 2025. The number of deaths remained unchanged at six. The other fatalities involved a nine-year-old boy and a four-year-old girl from Barangay Mansilingan, an eight-year-old boy from Barangay 16, a five-year-old girl from Barangay Granada, and an eight-year-old girl from Barangay Villamonte. Discover more Regional news subscription Western Visayas news Local event coverage CHO records showed that Barangay Mansilingan had the highest number of dengue cases, with 105, followed by Handumanan with 77 and Estefania with 73. Other barangays with high case counts were Alijis, with 58; Granada, 55; Villamonte and Taculing, 54 each; Singcang-Airport, 53; Tangub, 44; and Banago, 39. Dr. Grace Tan, head of the CHO’s Environmental Sanitation Division, urged residents experiencing fever and flu-like symptoms to seek early medical consultation. She also reminded the public to remain vigilant against dengue and follow the Department of Health’s 4S strategy: search for and destroy mosquito-breeding sites; secure self-protection against mosquito bites; seek early consultation; and support fogging and spraying in areas where these are warranted. Meanwhile, CHO Assistant Department Head Dr. Grace Tan also emphasized the importance of sustained household and community efforts to eliminate mosquito-breeding grounds. Residents were encouraged to practice the city’s “4Ts” of dengue prevention: Taob, Taktak, Tuyo and Takip — turn over water containers, discard accumulated water, keep containers dry, and cover water-storage vessels. The city also urged households to participate in its daily 4 p.m. cleanup habit to remove stagnant water and other potential mosquito-breeding sites. Health authorities advised residents to watch for dengue symptoms, including sudden high fever, severe headache, muscle and joint pain, pain behind the eyes, weakness and skin rashes. Discover more Environment news report Health wellness tips Business news updates Persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, unusual bleeding, dark-colored stools and difficulty breathing are warning signs that require immediate medical attention. The CHO stressed that dengue can progress rapidly and become life-threatening, making early consultation, close monitoring and prompt medical intervention essential to preventing severe complications and deaths./PN RELATED ARTICLESMORE FROM AUTHOR Region Bacolod releases P13.6M MassKara subsidies for participating barangays, schools Region Woman’s body found in sack in Talisay; 2 suspects arrested Region Molo lodging house room boy dies; police rule out foul play LEAVE A REPLY Cancel reply Please enter your comment! Subscribe Health News Florida Tampa officials go door-to-door to share dengue info in 5 hotspot neighborhoods WUSF | By Emma Brisk Published October 12, 2026 at 5:00 AM EDT Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Email Listen • 1:37 Emma Brisk / WUSF Code enforcement officers Josh Trimper, left, and David Daubar, right, translate an informative dengue fever flyer to a Spanish-speaking Forest Lake resident on Friday, Oct. 9, 2026. The city canvassed urged residents to dump out any standing water, which is how the Aedes aegypti mosquitoes responsible for the virus breed. Most of the breeding spots are abandoned tires. The Florida Department of Health reports the number of locally acquired dengue fever cases in Hillsborough County continue to rise – with 259 confirmed cases since July, which is 36 higher than the previous week’s numbers. Chelsea Kendrick is the epidemiology program manager with the Hillsborough County Health Department. She said the number of cases are likely higher, since only one in four people exposed to the virus show symptoms. ALSO READ: Hillsborough, Pinellas add to dengue tally as mosquito fight continues “We want residents to really look out for fever, headache, nausea or vomiting, and muscle or joint pain," she said. That’s why inspectors and code enforcement officers from the city of Tampa went door-to-door Friday to spread information in five neighborhoods with higher counts of the virus. Emma Brisk / WUSF David Daubar and other Tampa code enforcement officers spent about five hours Friday, Oct. 9, 2026, canvassing neighborhoods that are hotspots for dengue fever. They warned residents and shared preventative measures they can take. They passed out flyers in Southeast Seminole Heights, North Hyde Park, West Tampa, Forest Hills and Sulphur Springs, urging residents to dump out any standing water, which is how the Aedes aegypti mosquitoes responsible for the virus breed. “By all means, we don't want any more breeding grounds for this dengue virus,” said Jack Ciucio, Tampa’s district supervisor of code enforcement. “It's out there, and it's spreading a lot quicker than we actually thought.” The city threw Mosquito Dunks – floating, doughnut-shaped tablets that kill mosquito larvae – into bodies of water. They can be used in any stagnant water, since they don’t harm other biosystems in the environment. Emma Brisk / WUSF Inspectors dropped these Mosquito Dunks into any large body of water they saw across the five neighborhoods they canvassed Friday, Oct. 9, 2026. These mosquito control pellets are safe for the environment and kill off most larvae. City officials warn that even a bottle cap of standing water that has been sitting out for a week is big enough for mosquitoes to breed. Their recommendations include: Empty or cover anything that could hold water outside your home. This includes buckets, toys, pools, birdbaths, trash or recycling containers, boat or car covers, roof gutters, coolers, pet dishes and tires. Apply insect repellent to any exposed skin and on your clothes. Use air conditioning and keep screens on all windows. If you have a body of water you can’t care for on your own, like an unkempt pool, Ciucio said the city will issue a notice to do so. If you don’t, the city could take you to court and put a lien on your property. “For the most part, whenever we issue notice to a property owner, they'll generally take care of it in a quicker manner,” Ciucio said. But most of the breeding grounds come from tires. “[It’s] kind of at the perfect time of the year, unfortunately, where we have a lot of rainfall,” Kendrick said. “These tires can hold large amounts of water.” ALSO READ: Amid dengue outbreak, mosquito control experts are wary of a wet winter fueled by El Niño Over the past three months, Tampa has removed 23 tons of tires – 17 tons were illegally dumped by tire shops, Ciucio said. He said people dump loads of tires at night, leading city officials to have to get out as quickly as possible the next morning to clean them up and prevent more potential breeding grounds. “There's no way of telling who dumped them unless there's cameras,” Ciucio said. The Department of Health has been monitoring 85 tire shops statewide, but only two in Tampa have received citations. Dengue fever is in season; a series of power poles are being relocated on Chu Van An Street; gold prices are experiencing slight fluctuations; ... these are some of the notable news items related to Ho Chi Minh City in newspapers this morning, October 9th. Báo Sài Gòn Giải phóng•09/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 Dengue fever is seasonal. According to Dai Doan Ket newspaper, dengue fever is in season in Ho Chi Minh City, with over 35,700 cases reported since the beginning of the year. At pediatric hospitals, many children are admitted in critical condition, even experiencing shock, gastrointestinal bleeding, or respiratory failure. According to the Ho Chi Minh City Center for Disease Control (HCDC), in week 39, the city recorded 1,491 cases of dengue fever, equivalent to the average of the previous four weeks. From the beginning of 2026 to week 39, the total number of cases is 35,714. Some areas with high numbers of cases per 100,000 people include Con Dao Special Zone, Chanh Phu Hoa, and Minh Thanh. The Intensive Care and Toxicology Department of Children's Hospital 1 is treating several severe cases of dengue fever. Experts affirm that dengue fever has different stages of progression. When a child's fever subsides, it's not important to stop monitoring; on the contrary, families need to continue observing the child's condition, especially from the 3rd to the 6th day of the illness. Associate Professor, Doctor Pham Van Quang expressed concern about the fact that many children are brought to the hospital quite late. By the time they are admitted, the children are already in severe shock, and some even have multiple organ damage and failure, making treatment more difficult. According to the Ho Chi Minh City Center for Disease Control (HCDC), in week 39, Ho Chi Minh City also recorded 1,538 cases of hand, foot, and mouth disease, a sharp increase of 63.8% compared to the average of the previous four weeks. The total number of hand, foot, and mouth disease cases accumulated from the beginning of 2026 to week 39 is 36,676. Communes and wards with a high number of hand, foot, and mouth disease cases per 100,000 people include Con Dao Special Zone, Binh Khanh, and Hiep Phuoc. Gold prices today at Mi Hong, SJC, PNJ, and DOJI. As of 8:30 AM this morning, gold prices in Ho Chi Minh City have fluctuated slightly. Today's gold prices in Ho Chi Minh City show a buy-sell spread of 1.5-4 million VND per ounce, depending on the type of gold and the trading unit. Gold price chart for Mi Hong, SJC, PNJ, and DOJI on October 9th. Image created with AI assistance. According to the Lao Dong Newspaper, at Mi Hong Company, SJC gold bars are listed at 141.3 million VND/ounce for buying and 142.8 million VND/ounce for selling. Gold rings are also listed at 141.3-142.8 million VND/ounce (buying - selling). At SJC Company, gold bars are listed at 140.8-143.8 million VND/ounce (buying - selling). Gold rings are listed at 140.8-143.83 million VND/ounce. At PNJ, gold bars are listed at 140.0-143.0 million VND/ounce, while gold rings are priced at 139.5-142.5 million VND/ounce. At DOJI, gold bars are listed at 140.0-143.0 million VND/ounce. Gold rings are priced at 139.0-143.0 million VND/ounce. The buy-sell spread for gold bars at Mi Hong is 1.5 million VND/ounce, while SJC, PNJ, and DOJI all have a spread of 3 million VND/ounce. For gold rings, the spread is 1.5 million VND/ounce at Mi Hong, 3.03 million VND/ounce at SJC, 3 million VND/ounce at PNJ, and 4 million VND/ounce at DOJI. DOJI gold rings have the highest buy-sell spread. People flock to the high-quality Vietnamese goods fair to "hunt" for discounted ceramics, vegetarian products, and more. The festival celebrating 30 years of high-quality Vietnamese products, themed "Pride and Continuation," is currently taking place at Le Van Tam Park, Tan Dinh Ward. You may also like According to Tuoi Tre Online Newspaper, the fair, with 200 booths offering a variety of promotional programs, attracted a large number of customers to experience and shop. Numerous customers choose to buy discounted ceramic products at the Minh Long Ceramics booth - Photo: N.TRÍ Specifically, with promotions applied to all products, including discounts of up to 30%, the booth of Thien Thanh Spice Company was consistently bustling. Similarly, with a discount policy of up to 30% and a fixed price for products such as bowls, cups, plates, glasses, etc., the Minh Long ceramics booth became lively thanks to the large number of customers immediately after the opening. Customers look for discounted vegetarian products at the Au Lac booth - Photo: N.TRÍ Meanwhile, with a 20% discount applied to over 200 products, from packaged to frozen, the vegetarian food stall of Au Lac Vegetarian Food Production and Trading Co., Ltd. also became bustling with customers browsing and inquiring about products. Similarly, numerous other brands such as Duy Anh Foods' vermicelli and noodles, Tan Nhien rice paper, Vinamilk milk, etc., also applied various promotional policies, discounts, buy-one-get-three deals, and more. Customers sample products at the booth of Thien Thanh Spice Company - Photo: N.XUAN The 30th Anniversary Festival of High-Quality Vietnamese Goods took place from October 8th to 11th with many activities, including experiential and shopping activities at the fair with over 200 booths. Businesses are recruiting en masse, and Ho Chi Minh City is organizing job fairs at 12 locations. The demand for recruitment by businesses in Ho Chi Minh City is expected to increase significantly. The city is organizing job fairs in October simultaneously at 12 locations. In the first nine months of the year, the Ho Chi Minh City Employment Service Center organized 163 job fairs. Photo: TUNG NGUYEN Speaking to Dan Tri Online Newspaper, a representative from the Employment Service Center of the Ho Chi Minh City Department of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs said that the unit is coordinating with relevant agencies to prepare for the Job Fair and Job Exchange in October 2026. This job exchange will be organized on a large scale, taking place simultaneously at 12 locations across Ho Chi Minh City on the morning of October 13th (from 7:30 AM to 11:30 AM). According to the Ho Chi Minh City Employment Service Center, this job fair aims to support unemployed workers, self-employed individuals, students, and others in accessing labor market information and finding suitable jobs. At the same time, the program also supports businesses in the city in recruiting personnel for production and business operations in the final months of the year. Notably, this job fair utilizes information technology, connecting online interviews between different locations, making it easier for businesses and job seekers in remote areas to connect and conduct interviews without extensive travel. The Ho Chi Minh City Employment Service Center expects the program to connect thousands of job seekers with businesses in need of recruitment. Relocating a series of power poles will make inner-city roads wider and more spacious. After a series of utility poles were removed from the road, the section of Chu Van An Street passing through Binh Thanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, has become less congested, creating favorable conditions for the construction unit to complete the road surface and organize traffic. Gia Dinh Power Company is relocating power poles along Chu Van An Street. On the morning of October 9th, a reporter from Tien Phong Newspaper observed that the utility poles that had previously been located in the middle of Chu Van An Street, in the Binh Thanh ward, had been relocated. The road, now free of the poles, is wider and more convenient for traffic. The relocation of the power poles began on October 7th. The old power poles on Chu Van An Street were removed, returning the site to the construction unit. The relocation of power poles on Chu Van An Street began on October 7th. In late February 2025, the People's Committee of the former Binh Thanh District commenced a project to upgrade and expand a road section approximately 600 meters long. The project has a total investment of over 1,067 billion VND, including nearly 982 billion VND for compensation and land clearance. According to the design, the road section will be widened to 23 meters, comprising 4 lanes. A drainage system, lighting, and landscaping will also be constructed simultaneously. Upon completion, the road surface will be approximately four times wider than its current width. Workers are securing sections of overhead power cables. According to the investor, after the relocation of the power poles is completed, the site will be handed over to continue laying the asphalt, installing guardrails and median strips, completing the road centerline, painting road markings, and organizing traffic lanes. The remaining work is expected to be completed around mid-November 2026. After the utility poles were relocated, Chu Van An Street became wider and more spacious. supplementary_news.content: Dinamani Kannada Prabha Samakalika Malayalam Cinema Express Indulgexpress Edexlive Oct 14, 2026 11:04 PM Subscribe E-PAPER INDIA WORLD STATES CITIES OPINION EXPLAINER BUSINESS SPORTS GOOD NEWS ENTERTAINMENT VIDEOS LIVE BLOG INDIA WORLD STATES CITIES OPINION EXPLAINER BUSINESS SPORTS GOOD NEWS ENTERTAINMENT VIDEOS LIVE BLOG Trending Links Asian Games 2026 TVS group Dakshina Kannada rename healthy food street food Advertisement Gujarat 87 hospitalised in Gujarat after Statue of Unity Parade as Dengue hits security personnel Special teams are also monitoring health and hygiene conditions at the camps, while specialist resident doctors have been deployed at Gandhinagar Civil Hospital to provide prompt treatment to the admitted personnel. The affected personnel belong to the Border Security Force (BSF), Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP). Representative Image/ Express Illustrations Dilip Singh Kshatriya Updated on: 09 Oct 2026, 12:11 pm 2 min read Copied AHMEDABAD: Dengue and other fever-related illnesses have affected security personnel who arrived in Gujarat for the Statue of Unity parade in Kevadia, with 87 admitted to Gandhinagar Civil Hospital over the past 10 days. Of them, 50 have recovered and been discharged, while 37 remain under treatment. Meanwhile, one jawan died during treatment after complaining of severe chest pain, with a suspected cardiac arrest being investigated as the cause of death. Health Minister Praful Pansheriya visited Gandhinagar Civil Hospital to assess the condition of the admitted personnel and review the medical arrangements. He met the patients, inquired about their health and held discussions with hospital superintendent Dr Mita Parikh and the treating doctors to ensure that adequate care was being provided. According to the minister, the affected personnel belong to the Border Security Force (BSF), Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP). They had arrived from Odisha, Jharkhand, Delhi, West Bengal and Chhattisgarh to participate in the parade organised at the Statue of Unity in Kevadia. They were shifted to the hospital after developing fever and other health complaints. Pansheriya said the condition of the 37 personnel still undergoing treatment was stable and improving, adding that none of them was in a critical condition. During the review, the minister directed hospital authorities to ensure uninterrupted treatment, adequate hydration and nutritious food for the personnel. He instructed the medical team to arrange fresh fruits, fruit juice, salads and a balanced diet in accordance with doctors' recommendations. He also reviewed the availability of blood and platelet stocks to meet any emergency requirements during dengue treatment. Emphasising the responsibility of the Health Department, Pansheriya said the personnel who safeguard the country's borders must receive the best possible care while recovering from illness. He directed the hospital administration to ensure that no lapses occurred in their treatment. The minister also expressed grief over the death of a security personnel who was undergoing treatment at the hospital. According to the preliminary account, the jawan suddenly complained of severe chest pain. Doctors conducted an electrocardiogram (ECG), shifted him to the intensive care unit and initiated emergency treatment. However, he could not be saved. Pansheriya said preliminary medical observations suggested that the jawan had continued his strenuous daily exercise routine despite suffering from fever and physical discomfort. This has raised the possibility of a cardiac event, although the exact cause of death remains unconfirmed. The minister said the suspected cardiac arrest or heart attack would have to be assessed in light of the medical findings. The final cause of death will be established after the post-mortem report is received. Meanwhile, the Health Department has intensified preventive measures at the accommodation sites where the security personnel are staying. Under the guidance of Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, departmental teams are carrying out fogging and insecticide spraying twice daily to control mosquito breeding and reduce the risk of further infections. Special teams are also monitoring health and hygiene conditions at the camps, while specialist resident doctors have been deployed at Gandhinagar Civil Hospital to provide prompt treatment to the admitted personnel. With 37 personnel still receiving medical care, the focus remains on their recovery, close monitoring and preventing further infections. The circumstances surrounding the jawan's death are also awaiting confirmation through the post-mortem findings.
